name: Riftbound TCG (League of Legends card game)
one_line: Physical/digital TCG where 1v1 matches are won by racing to 8 points scored only by conquering (taking a battlefield you don't already control) or holding (controlling one at the start of your turn) contested battlefields.
take_what: Score points ONLY from contested/enemy-adjacent territory, never from your own uncontested corner: 'conquer' = take a zone you didn't control this turn (1pt), 'hold' = still control it at start of next turn (1pt). This makes turtling in your own zone worthless - you MUST cross into contested ground to score at all.
constraint: none - abstract scoring pattern, not proprietary content

name: Konkr.io
one_line: Free browser hex territory-capture strategy game (Phaser-based, 2025 feature on Phaser.io) inspired by Slay: expand provinces, capture enemy hexes when your unit's strength exceeds every defender's strength.
take_what: Strict strength/threshold capture rule (attacker strength must exceed EVERY defending tile's strength, not just net) plus province-wide income: each connected province earns 1 coin per tile per turn, banked at towns - so bigger stable territory funds more/stronger pushes, creating a snowball that pressures players to contest borders early before opponents outscale them.

name: Manahex
one_line: 2024-25 hex-board fantasy TCG (Steam/itch, by Erik Svedäng) for 2-4 players: move your mage onto an adjacent hex to take control of it, and each hex's color/type generates the specific mana used to cast that turn's spells/creatures/buildings.
take_what: Board position IS the resource: controlled hexes generate typed mana on the spot (no separate mana pool/land-drop system), so every tile you place or move onto has an immediate, visible payoff tied to color-matching - collapsing 'build economy' and 'place tile' into one legible action.
constraint: none - mechanism is generic resource-on-tile pattern

name: ShoreTiles
one_line: 2026 PC tile-placement strategy game with a day/night cycle: build and place tiles freely by day, then at night the sea turns hostile and creatures converge on your lighthouse, forcing defensive tile layout under time pressure.
take_what: Alternating build-phase/threat-phase rhythm plus a permanent-decision rule (no undo on tile placement) that makes every placement feel weighty; the night phase is the 'wow moment' - passive building suddenly becomes a visible, escalating attack wave that tests your layout.
constraint: none - single-player PvE pattern, would need reimagining for 1v1

name: Kings of Osaro
one_line: Indie hex-tiled turn-based strategy game (itch.io, dev 'Trep') combining faction command with TCG-style cards, commanding ancient factions on a hex board.
take_what: Direct genre neighbor (hex board + TCG cards + faction identity) worth deep-diving for its specific card/tile interface choices, but page lacked enough public detail to extract a concrete mechanism - flagged for a follow-up deep-crawl pass rather than a take here.
constraint: needs direct playtest/deeper crawl - public info too thin to confirm specifics

name: HEXBLOOM
one_line: Solarpunk roguelite hex-strategy game about restoring a ruined ecosystem tile by tile, tagged alongside card-game/hex-based titles on itch.io.
take_what: Ecosystem-restoration framing turns tile placement into a visible before/after transformation (ruined -> bloomed) rather than abstract number math - a candidate pattern for giving Limen's tile placement more legible visual feedback per problem (2).
constraint: solo PvE game, mechanism needs adaptation for 1v1 duel context

name: BGDF: Incentivizing Aggressiveness (design forum thread)
one_line: Board Game Designers Forum thread cataloguing concrete mechanisms used across published games to force early player conflict instead of parallel corner-turtling.
take_what: Named mechanisms: (a) maintenance/upkeep economies that punish passive accumulation and force expansion into contested space, (b) territory value that depreciates the longer it's held uncontested (kills 'sit in my corner' as a viable line), (c) risk/reward skew where the first aggressor can claim enough resource lead that non-aggression becomes a losing strategy.
constraint: none - generic design theory, safe to adapt

name: Konkr.io on Phaser.io feature
one_line: Phaser.io's May 2025 feature on Konkr.io as a browser-native hex strategy success story, covering its 'easy to learn, hard to master' design goal and AI opponent design.
take_what: AI opponent uses a two-stage evaluation: heuristics first generate a shortlist of plausible candidate moves, then a slower full utility function scores only that shortlist - a cheap pattern for giving Limen a credible AI/bot opponent (relevant if solo/practice mode is ever needed) without brute-forcing the full hex move space.
